note: Extracted from the authoritative design source. Generated; do not edit by hand. Regenerate with: npm run design:extract
authority: veyro-product-experience-design/ is the single authoritative source for frontend design. ds.json carries Step 2 only; this file carries Steps 3, 4 and 5.

Button.label: string (required, verb-first)
rules: lg (44px) is mandatory in Touch and Spacious density -- the minimum target, not a style.
sm is Compact-only and never appears on Coach, Member, Front Desk or Kiosk.
One primary per view. Not per card, per view.
Destructive is never adjacent to primary.
Label is verb first, object second, no gerunds. Amounts belong in destructive and financial labels so the confirm reads the consequence.
One shell for all eighteen field types; a new type is a control swap, not a component.
The message slot holds exactly one message: error > warning > success > description.
Validate on blur, never on keystroke; re-validate on submit.
Required is marked, optional is not -- whichever is rarer gets the mark.
Financial forms state the consequence above the submit, not in a dialog after it.
Four severities, not five: success is not a severity, it is the neutral case.
The component takes an enum, not a string, so an engineer cannot invent a status.
Never colour alone -- every badge carries its label; icon-only status is a defect.
The edge-mark carries the row-level roll-up; the badge names the specific state.

common_mistakes: A status rendered by colour alone
A shadow on a table row
A dialog on a one-step-undoable action
A disabled control a role can never enable
A bare number with no money kind

grid_states.treatment: Skeleton rows at the real row height, header already solid, count as “loading…”. Never a centred spinner — layout must not jump when data lands.
Explains what the view will contain and offers the action that creates the first record. “No members yet — import your existing list or add one.”
Names the filters causing it and offers to clear them. Never implies the records do not exist.
“You do not have access to members at Abdoun.” Distinct from filtered-empty, because implying absence when the cause is authorization is a lie.
Rows render; a header strip states what is stale and how stale. “Retail figures are 20 minutes behind.”
Keeps whatever loaded, states what failed and offers retry. Never replaces a populated grid with an error page.
Cell reads “restricted” in tertiary text, not blank and not zero. A blank money cell reads as JOD 0.00 and that is a financial misstatement.
Selection locks, a progress state replaces the bulk bar, rows already processed mark individually. Cancellable, with completed work retained.
Grid marks itself cached with the age of the data; write actions in the bulk bar disable with the reason stated.

overlays.name: Modal
overlays.rules: Max one depth. Financial and destructive variants show the consequence summary above the confirm. Mobile: full-screen sheet with the action pinned. Never for a form longer than one screen.

overlays.name: Drawer
overlays.rules: Right side (inline-end), 380–480px, does not block the list behind it. The Member 360 pattern generalised. Mobile: becomes a full-screen push view with back.

overlays.name: Sheet
overlays.rules: Two levels maximum. Swipe-to-dismiss plus a visible close. Primary action in the lower third. Height fits content up to 80vh, then scrolls internally.

overlays.name: Card
overlays.rules: Six kinds: informational, interactive, summary, media, person, booking. A card that only draws a border around a paragraph is deleted — “cardification” of every screen is explicitly prohibited.

overlays.name: Banner
overlays.rules: Inline (one field or row), page (this screen), global (the whole tenant — outage, billing, integration). Critical banners are not dismissible while the condition holds. Max one global at a time.

overlays.name: Toast
overlays.rules: 30s undo window, one at a time, never carries information needed after dismissal. If the user must act on it, it is a banner or a task.

overlays.name: Tabs
overlays.rules: Five maximum. Never a substitute for information architecture — Member 360 uses a section rail plus a timeline spine, not fifteen tabs. Mobile: horizontally scrollable with no arrows.

overlays.name: SegmentedControl
overlays.rules: Short labels only. Switches how the same content is presented, never what content is shown. Mobile-safe at 44px.

contracts.accessibility: Accessible name in both languages even when icon-only. Loading sets aria-busy and keeps the label — never replaced by a spinner alone. Never a link styled as a button.
contracts.rtl: Icon side swaps with logical start/end. Chevrons and arrows mirror; check, clock, play do not.
contracts.responsive: lg (44px) mandatory in Touch and Spacious. fullWidth in sheets and mobile forms.

contracts.accessibility: Label is a real label, not a placeholder. Error text referenced by the field and read on focus. Prefix and suffix are decorative and excluded from the accessible name.
contracts.rtl: Text aligns to logical start; numbers, phone, currency and IDs are bidi-isolated. Prefix moves to the inline-start edge.
contracts.responsive: Full width below bp.sm. Numeric keyboards on number, currency, phone. Sheet lifts so the primary action stays visible above the keyboard.

contracts.accessibility: One composite tab stop with arrow navigation. Header announced once, then row content with position. Sort state announced on change. Money read with its kind.
contracts.rtl: Column order mirrors; numeric and money columns stay end-aligned on the logical end. Sort arrows mirror. Row expansion chevron mirrors.
contracts.responsive: Column priority 1–3; drops 3 then 2. Becomes a PersonRow list at bp.xs with the sort key as the secondary line. Never horizontally scrolled on a phone.

contracts.accessibility: One tab stop, arrows follow visual direction. Announces weekday, date, relation and availability. Unavailable dates state the reason, not just disabled.
contracts.rtl: Days mirror, weeks do not. Prev/next mirror in icon and position. Week start from market token. Numerals from tenant setting, grid sized for the widest form.
contracts.responsive: Inline on desktop, sheet below bp.sm. Range shows two months side by side above bp.md, one month with a scroll below.

contracts.accessibility: Focus trapped, Esc closes, results are a listbox with aria-activedescendant. Result class announced when it changes. Action previews are read in full before confirmation.
contracts.rtl: Text and results align to logical start; keyboard hints mirror position. Latin shortcuts stay LTR inside Arabic labels.
contracts.responsive: Full-screen below bp.sm with the input pinned to the top and the keyboard accounted for. Recents replace results on empty query.

contracts.accessibility: Focus moves to the modal, trapped until dismissed, returns to the trigger. Title is the accessible name. Esc closes unless the action is destructive and mid-flight.
contracts.rtl: Layout mirrors; the primary action sits at the logical end of the footer.
contracts.responsive: Becomes a full-screen sheet below bp.sm with the primary action pinned above the safe area.

contracts.accessibility: Same trap-and-return as modal, but the list behind stays readable and its scroll position is preserved on close.
contracts.rtl: Opens from the inline-end edge — right in LTR, left in RTL.
contracts.responsive: Overlay at bp.md, full-screen push view below bp.sm with a back affordance.

contracts.accessibility: Focus trap, swipe and button dismissal both available. Two levels maximum; a third is a design error.
contracts.rtl: Content mirrors; drag handle is centred and direction-neutral.
contracts.responsive: Mobile only. Above bp.md the same content is a Drawer or Modal.

contracts.accessibility: Label always present, never colour alone. Severity is in the text, not only the hue. Not a button unless it opens something.
contracts.rtl: Label mirrors with the row. Severity edge-mark moves to the logical start edge.
contracts.responsive: Label may abbreviate at Compact but never disappear. Full text in the accessible name regardless.

contracts.accessibility: Roving tabindex, arrows move, Home/End jump, selected announced. Panel associated with its tab.
contracts.rtl: Order mirrors; overflow scroll direction mirrors. Underline indicator follows the logical position.
contracts.responsive: Horizontally scrollable below bp.sm with no arrow buttons — arrows on a touch surface are a desktop habit.

contracts.accessibility: role=status for info and success, role=alert only for critical. Never both — an alert interrupts, and most banners should not.
contracts.rtl: Icon and text mirror; the severity bar sits on the logical start edge.
contracts.responsive: Stacks above content at every breakpoint. Global banner is fixed and does not scroll away.

contracts.accessibility: Polite live region. Undo is keyboard-reachable for the full 30 seconds and not dismissed by pointer movement.
contracts.rtl: Slides from the logical end. Text mirrors.
contracts.responsive: Bottom-centre on mobile above the nav; bottom inline-end on desktop.

docs.requirement: Present many records so a user can scan, compare, select and act without leaving the view.
Any list of more than about ten records where comparison across fields matters, or where bulk action is a real workflow.
Fewer than ten records with no comparison need — use a list. Records with rich media or a single dominant attribute — use cards. A single record — use Member 360.
SavedViewBar · FilterBar · header row · rows · cells (text, money, status, person, date, action) · BulkActionBar · pagination or virtual scroll · column config.
selectable | readonly · with inspector | standalone · virtual | paginated · grouped | flat.
The nine in §04 plus the eleven in the §09 matrix. Required: loading, three empties, partial, error, restricted cell, bulk in progress, offline.

Sort single-column, persisted per saved view. Selection survives sort and filter within a session, and the count always states what is selected. Inline actions appear on row focus or hover, never permanently — a permanent action column costs the width the data needs.
Column headers are nouns, not sentences. Money cells always carry currency and kind. Dates are relative under seven days ("19d ago") and absolute beyond. Never a bare number in a money column.
See the §10 contract. Additionally: selection announced as a count, not per row, when a range is selected.
See the §10 contract. Additionally: mixed Arabic and Latin names sort by the tenant collation, and both spellings are searchable.
See the §10 contract. Additionally: column config is a sheet below bp.sm and saved views collapse into a single select.

Shrinking the desktop grid onto a phone · a permanent actions column · colour-only status · blank cells for restricted data · reporting "done" after a bulk action · a shadow on a row · putting the primary action in the header where it competes with sort.

patterns.name: Attention queue
patterns.components: Header with counts · AttentionRow list · empty-success state · new-items pill.
patterns.rule: Sorted by severity then money then age, never recency. Never reshuffles under a reading user. This is the Command Center and the Coach Today screen — one pattern, two surfaces.

patterns.name: List → inspector
patterns.components: DataGrid or PersonRow list · Drawer inspector · timeline spine inside.
patterns.rule: Two panes, never three. The list keeps its scroll and selection when the inspector closes. Member 360, lead detail, invoice detail and staff detail are all this — the Phase 6 decision, generalised.

patterns.name: Capture → resolve
patterns.components: Fixed capture strip (scan or search) · result area · focus returns to capture.
patterns.rule: Front Desk and POS. After every action focus goes back to the scan field, because the next member is already at the desk. One modal depth maximum.

patterns.name: Guided sale
patterns.components: Cart · member · payment method · receipt choice · done. Inline, one screen.
patterns.rule: Never a wizard. Membership sale, PT package and retail differ only in cart contents. Tax and terms visible before payment, never after.

patterns.name: Assisted create
patterns.components: Context · generate or template · adjust inline · preview · assign.
patterns.rule: Workout and nutrition plan creation. The machine drafts, the human edits in place — no second editor, no blank page. Two unknowns asked, never twelve knowns.

patterns.name: One-tap log
patterns.components: Pre-filled value · single 44px primary · adjust affordance · offline-safe write.
patterns.rule: Set logging, meal logging, check-in, session completion. Adjustment available, never required. Writes locally first and says so.

patterns.name: Bulk act
patterns.components: Select · action bar · preview of scope · progress · partial-result breakdown.
patterns.rule: Never reports “done”. Always reports what did not happen and why, with each group as an actionable filtered selection.

patterns.name: Ask → evidence → act
patterns.components: Question · answer with linked evidence · proposed action · human confirms.
patterns.rule: Every AI surface. Marked, evidenced, never auto-executing, confidence in words. Financial and destructive actions excluded.

patterns.name: Scoped compare
patterns.components: Scope switcher (searchable, grouped, multi-select) · aligned metric rows · variance.
patterns.rule: Chain reporting. Never a dropdown of 50 clubs. Always states the scope in the chrome so “which club is this” never needs a click.

patterns.name: Approval request
patterns.components: Requestable control · request with reason · approver queue · outcome notification.
patterns.rule: The third permission state made concrete. Over-threshold refunds, long freezes, policy exceptions. Keeps authority intact without making the requester phone someone.

tiers.applies_to: Sending a message, assigning a task, changing a filter, logging a set, completing a session, most edits — 19 of the 31 audited.
tiers.why: Reversible within seconds and low-consequence. A dialog here trains dismissal and buys nothing.

tiers.applies_to: Cancelling a booking inside its window, removing a cart line, unassigning a coach — 7 of 31.
tiers.why: Not cleanly reversible but not costly. A one-line “Cancel Dana's 18:00?” in place beats a modal that steals the screen.

tiers.applies_to: Refunds, membership cancellation, destructive plan changes, sensitive exports, biometric removal.
tiers.why: Real money, real records, or a person's data. States what happens, to whom, and what cannot be undone. The amount goes in the button.

tiers.applies_to: Over-threshold refunds, freezes beyond policy, permission grants, bulk exports of member data.
tiers.why: The actor may not hold the authority. More typing would not fix that — a second human, or a re-authentication, is the only honest control.

cross.rule: Every action reachable without a pointer. Composite widgets are one tab stop with arrow navigation inside — a 14-row grid costs one stop, not fourteen.
System-owned 2px ring with a 1px offset, never brand-configurable, never removed on mouse users.
Overlays trap focus and return it to the trigger. Route changes move focus to the heading, not the body.
Landmarks on every surface. Live regions polite for confirmations, assertive only for genuine alerts. Money read with its kind; status read as text.
Every status carries a label. Severity is edge-mark and chip and wording. Charts state direction in words.
44px minimum in Touch and Spacious; 32px floor in Compact desktop where a pointer is guaranteed.
Layouts hold to 200% zoom and to iOS Dynamic Type XXL without clipping or horizontal scroll.
All durations to 0 except an 80ms opacity crossfade. Rest timers become numeric countdowns; AI text still streams because streaming is the information.
Logical properties throughout — no left/right in any component. Mirroring is per-element, from the icon manifest.
Days mirror, weeks do not. Range fields keep reading order. Mono columns switch family but keep width. Timelines mirror direction but not chronology.
Money, phone, IDs, card last-four, times and Latin names each isolated. Enforced at the formatter, not per component.
+0.15 line-height, 13px floor, weight up one step, zero tracking, containers sized from the Arabic string.
Five, with declared behaviour per surface. Tables become lists below bp.xs; they are never horizontally scrolled on a phone.
Four modes changing row height, spacing step and type step only. Colour, radius, anatomy and hierarchy are invariant.

platform.web: CSS custom properties generated from the JSON source.
platform.ios: SwiftUI Color/Font extensions with Dynamic Type mappings.
platform.android: Compose theme values with sp/dp scaling.

platform.web: Rail plus routes; browser back is authoritative.
platform.ios: Tab bar, navigation stack, native back and edge swipe.
platform.android: Bottom nav, predictive back, up navigation.

platform.ios: UISheetPresentation with detents; full-screen for destructive flows.
platform.android: Bottom sheet with drag handle; dialog for tier 3.

platform.ios: Native list with cell reuse; swipe actions for tier 1 undo only.

platform.web: Keyboard-wedge and USB scanners on Front Desk.
platform.ios: Camera with haptic on success; NFC for access passes.
platform.android: CameraX with the same haptic contract.

platform.web: Service worker cache; queued writes with visible pending count.
platform.ios: Local store with background sync; pending count in the tab badge.
platform.android: Room with WorkManager; same badge contract.

platform.ios: Success on log and check-in; warning on denial. Never on navigation.
VoiceOver traits, Dynamic Type, Reduce Motion honoured.
platform.android: TalkBack, font scale, animator duration scale honoured.

pay_states.copy: Amount, method, timestamp. No green badge — paid is the expected case and colouring it makes the unpaid row harder to find.
“Sent to the bank, usually clears within an hour.” Never “processing” alone — a duration prevents the second attempt that causes a double charge.
Reason in plain words (“the card expired”), what was NOT affected (“access is unchanged”), and the single recovery action. Never a provider error code as the headline.
Attempt number, next attempt time, and how to stop it. A silent retry loop is how a member gets charged three times.
Amount, days late, and whether access is affected under this tenant's policy — the answer differs per tenant and must never be inferred by the reader.
Signed amount, destination, arrival window, reason, and who authorised it. All five, always.
Both figures side by side — original and refunded — never a single net number that hides what happened.
What the member claims, the evidence deadline, and who owns the response. Time-boxed, so the deadline is the loudest element.
“Collected at the desk, not yet reconciled.” Distinguishes a drawer variance from a real shortfall at close.
Credit used and remaining balance, both visible. A wallet with an invisible balance is a support ticket.

families.name: PersonRow
families.anatomy: Photo · name · membership or role · context line · status · one action. Four densities, four subjects: member, lead, coach, staff.
families.decision: One component, not four. Behaviour is identical — identify a person, see their state, act once — so ClientCard and MemberCard would be the same thing with different words. The subject only changes which context line renders.

families.name: TimelineItem
families.anatomy: Time · actor · event · amount or object · expandable detail. Types: payment, visit, booking, session, message, note, plan change, document, consent.
families.decision: One spine, chronological, filterable by type — the Member 360 decision generalised. The actor is always named, including “Veyro” for automated events, because “who did this” is the question a timeline exists to answer.

families.name: MembershipCard
families.anatomy: Plan · status · period · price · renewal terms · freeze allowance used. Variants: active, trial, frozen, expiring, expired, cancelled.
families.decision: Renewal terms are always visible, never behind a link — the single most common member dispute is what they thought they signed up for. Freeze allowance shows used-of-total, so a refusal is never a surprise.

families.name: BookingCard
families.anatomy: Class or session · time · coach · location · capacity · member state. Variants: confirmed, waitlisted, cancelled, no-show, full, in progress.
families.decision: Waitlist shows position and honest odds (“3rd on the list — usually clears”). Cancellation states the deadline and what happens after it, on the card, before the member commits.

families.name: AccessPass
families.anatomy: QR or NFC · member name · validity · club. States: valid, expiring today, expired, restricted, offline-cached.
families.decision: Renders offline from cache and says so with a timestamp. A member at a turnstile with no signal is the normal case, not an edge case.

families.name: TaskRow
families.anatomy: Owner · due · subject · source · one action. Variants: assigned, self-created, from an exception, overdue.
families.decision: Every task names where it came from — an exception, a person, an automation. An orphan task with no provenance gets ignored, which is how a queue dies.

families.name: PlanBuilderRow
families.anatomy: Day or meal slot · content · macros or volume · alternatives count · lock state.
families.decision: The coach edits in place; nothing opens a second editor. Locked rows show why they are locked (policy, member allergy, medical note) rather than being merely disabled.

families.name: ConsentBlock
families.anatomy: Purpose · scope · granted date · granting party · withdraw action. Types: marketing, health data, biometric, photo, minor guardian.
families.decision: Health and biometric consent are separate records with separate withdrawal, never bundled into a terms checkbox. Withdrawal is always one action from where the consent is shown — never a support request.

families.name: StaffAvailability
families.anatomy: Coach · hours · qualifications · current load · conflicts. Variants: available, partial, full, off, unqualified for this class.
families.decision: “Unqualified” is a distinct state from “unavailable” and says which qualification is missing. Assigning an unqualified coach to a class is a safety issue, not a scheduling inconvenience.

jordan.copy: “Sent to JoFotara · reference JF-88214.” Reference visible immediately, because that is what an accountant is asked for.
Quiet confirmation on the invoice with the timestamp. No banner — acceptance is the expected case.
The specific field at fault, in plain words (“missing buyer tax number”), plus the assurance that the sale and the money are recorded. Fix-and-resubmit is one action.
“JoFotara is not responding. Invoices are queued and will submit automatically — nothing is lost, and you can keep selling.” Selling never blocks on e-invoicing.
Alias shown, amount shown, “waiting for the member to confirm in their bank app” with a live elapsed timer. Staff know whether to wait or move on.
Matched to the member and the order, with the bank reference retained on the invoice for reconciliation.
“A JOD 55.00 transfer arrived that we could not match.” Sits in a reconciliation queue with the reference and the sender alias — never silently discarded, never auto-assigned to a guess.
The request timed out; the cart is preserved and another method is offered. The member is not charged and is told so.

character: The system shows its reasoning. Evidence links, confidence, and “here is why” live in the type hierarchy rather than in badges announcing cleverness.
Few colours, generous type scale contrast, no decoration compensating for weak hierarchy. Nothing on screen is hedging.
Hairlines over shadows, 34px rows where the work is, mono numerals that align without effort. Speed is a visual property here, not just a performance one.
Warm paper neutrals, semantic colour held in reserve, one accent. A busy Tuesday at Khalda should not look like an emergency.
Earned through restraint, alignment and consistency — the same way a well-set financial statement reads expensive without ornament.
Editorial scale and plain-language copy for member moments; no mascots, no exclamation marks, no emoji in the product.
Mono for data, sans for speech. Warm greys rather than clinical blue-white — this is a business about bodies, not a laboratory.
No black-and-neon, no shouting weights, no motivational bombast. Strength shown through precision.
semantic: App background. The field everything sits on.
Table headers, inset wells, code and log areas.
Row and interactive-surface hover only. Never a resting state.
Selected row, active nav item, chosen segment.
Field backgrounds across all form controls.
Headings, values, member names, primary content.
Metadata, timestamps, IDs, eyebrow labels. Contrast floor for small text.
Inactive controls only. Always paired with a stated reason.
On filled action and semantic surfaces.
Overdue amounts, failed states, destructive labels.
Row dividers inside a bounded container.
Container edges, inputs, table outlines. The workhorse.
Invalid field outline, paired with a message.
Primary button fill, active selection, links.
Expiring, approaching a limit, needs review.
Neutral system information. Deliberately not the action hue.
AI interpretation, recommendation, evidence and executed-action states. SYSTEM-OWNED — never inherits brand.accent. 9.31:1 on warm.0.
AI panel header and evidence-link background. The only wash that signals machine reasoning.
AI container edge. Distinguishes an interpretation panel from an action panel at a glance.
themes: Eight hours of tabular reading. Hairline rules and mono columns separate best on a light field, and warm paper is easier at length than a bright white. Dark ships as an opt-in for late shifts, not as a default, and is validated on the data grid before release.

Lobbies are bright, the screen is read at 1.5m, and staff do not choose their lighting. Dark would cost contrast headroom at exactly the moment resolution speed matters. A deliberate omission, not a gap.
Gym-floor lighting swings from window glare to dim free-weight corners. This is the surface where user control genuinely earns its keep — and the set logger is validated in both.
Consumer expectation, plus evening and pre-dawn training sessions. Dark is a first-class member experience here, not a courtesy.
Same reasoning as Admin, with incident work often happening at night — which is precisely when the opt-in gets used.
type_scale: Member milestones, first-run, progress reviews. The editorial register from 1c. Never on Admin.
Section heading, modal title, member name in a 360 header.
Dense group heading inside a panel.
Member app body, coach prose, explanatory paragraphs.
Default. Admin content, descriptions, table text.
Secondary explanation, helper text under a field.
Field labels, button text, chips, nav items.
Legal, footnotes, timestamps. Latin only — Arabic floor is 13.
Mono tabular. Money, counts, sets, reps, macros, IDs. The reason columns align.
Mono uppercase section markers. Latin only.
arabic_rules: At any given size, Arabic gets 0.15 more line-height than Latin — type.body is 1.60 in Latin and 1.75 in Arabic. Diacritics and descenders need the room, and dense Arabic without it is the single most common failure in localised SaaS.
Arabic never renders below 13px. type.caption (11) and type.eyebrow (10) are Latin-only tokens; their Arabic counterparts resolve to 13px. A caption that cannot be read is not a caption.

Plex Sans Arabic reads optically lighter than Plex Sans at the same weight. Where Latin uses 400, Arabic uses 400; where Latin uses 450 or 500, Arabic uses 500; where Latin uses 500 for emphasis, Arabic uses 600.
Never apply tracking to Arabic — it breaks the joins. Any token carrying a track value drops it in Arabic, which is why type.eyebrow has no Arabic form and uses type.label instead.
Arabic has no italic convention. Emphasis is weight or colour. Any component using italics for meaning must have a non-italic Arabic path.

Arabic runs 15–30% longer than English here. Every label container, button and column is dimensioned against the Arabic string, not the English one. Design reviews use the Arabic build for width decisions.
IBM Plex Mono has no Arabic. Tabular Arabic numerals use Plex Sans Arabic with tabular figures; a mono column in an Arabic table switches family but keeps its alignment and width.
Latin or Arabic-Indic, chosen once per tenant and applied identically on screen, receipt, export and PDF. Never mixed within a tenant, and never decided per component.

Money, phone numbers, member IDs, card last-four, times and Latin lift names are each wrapped in an isolated run. Without it JOD jumps to the wrong side of its amount — a money-ambiguity defect, not a typographic one.
contrast: Pass everywhere, all sizes. AAA on all three.
Pass on warm.0 and warm.100 — the small-text floor. FAILS on warm.150 by 0.02: large-text-only there, and the pairing is excluded from the CI allow-list.
FAIL under 18.66px on every surface. Large text, disabled controls and decoration only.
Pass. Also passes inverse — white on ink.600 is 10.21:1.
Pass. White on error.600 is 7.70:1 for filled badges.
Pass. The tightest semantic — do not lighten. White on fill is 5.89:1.
Pass as text and as a filled surface — white on fill is 7.64:1.
Pass all sizes. White on ai.600 is 9.38:1. Distinct from ink.600 (10.13:1) by hue, not lightness — the two never share a role.

breakpoints.name: bp.xs
breakpoints.behaviour: Single column. Bottom nav of five. Sheets replace modals. Tables become drill-down lists, never shrunken grids.

breakpoints.name: bp.sm
breakpoints.behaviour: Tablet portrait. Coach gains a two-pane client list. Front Desk minimum. Rail collapses to icons.

breakpoints.name: bp.md
breakpoints.behaviour: Tablet landscape and small laptop. Admin usable: rail collapsed, inspector becomes an overlay rather than a column.

breakpoints.name: bp.lg
breakpoints.behaviour: Admin target. Rail expanded at 240, content and inspector side by side.

breakpoints.name: bp.xl
breakpoints.behaviour: Wide desktop. Content caps at 1440 and centres; the inspector widens to 480 rather than the table stretching indefinitely.

layouts.specification: 12-column, 24px gutter. Rail 240 expanded / 56 collapsed. Content max 1440. Inspector 380 at bp.lg, 480 at bp.xl. Split view is list + inspector, never three columns — the Member 360 decision from Phase 6 generalised.

Two zones, no rail: a fixed capture strip at the top holding scan and search, and a resolution area below. Touch density, one modal depth maximum, keyboard focus returning to the scan field after every action.
Single column, bottom nav of four plus a create action. Sheets capped at two levels. Primary actions in the lower third for one-handed reach. Two-pane only from bp.sm on tablet.
Single column, Spacious. Bottom nav of five. One “now” card owning the top of the viewport; everything else below the fold. Sheets for swap, filter and quick choices.
Same shell as Admin at Compact density, with an incident banner slot above the rail that no other surface has.

brandable: One hue, replacing ink.600 for action and selection. The derived pressed, selected-wash and dark-mode variants are computed by the system, not configured — six tokens from one input.
Wordmark and mark, each with a required monochrome fallback for receipts, exports and single-colour contexts. Clear-space and minimum size enforced.
Member app icon per brand, validated against store requirements at upload.
Photography for member home, class listings and store. Aspect ratios fixed by the system; content is the tenant’s.
Optional, one step softer or sharper across the whole scale. Proportional — a tenant cannot round only the cards. Off by default.
guardrails: G1
brand.accent must reach 4.5:1 against surface.default and surface.canvas, and its computed on-accent label colour must reach 4.5:1 against the accent itself.
Rejected at upload with the nearest passing shade of their own colour offered, shown side by side. They are never left without a route to a brand they recognise.
G2
brand.accent must sit a minimum perceptual distance from success, warning and error. A brand green close to success.600 fails.
“This green is too close to the colour Veyro uses for confirmed payments.” Alternative offered, with the reason stated in operational terms rather than colour theory.
G3
brand.accent may never resolve into a status, money-state, safety or consent token. Enforced by the token boundary — the accent is simply not in scope for those components.
Not surfaced, because it cannot be attempted. This is the difference between a guardrail and a guideline.
G4
The focus ring is system-owned in both themes.
Not configurable. A tenant cannot ship an unnavigable product.
G5
Dark-mode accent is derived from brand.accent, not configured separately.
